messages.content: Quick Phoenix pre-trip check: I leave Monday. The client says they will shuttle me from the hospital campus to the Scottsdale walkthrough Wednesday, but the return time is still approximate. Online check-in opens soon. Anything worth changing?

The plan still looks sound. I would not change the flight times: the nonstop keeps the least exposure with Atlanta weather unsettled, and leaving Decatur around 7:45 still gives you a reasonable buffer for the late-morning departure. At check-in, keep 24A outbound if it is same cabin/no fee, and keep 31F on the return unless a better window opens.
Hotel reconfirmed luggage storage, on-site dinner, and paid breakfast only. Any issue with that for Monday or Thursday?

No issue. Monday, the on-site dinner keeps the arrival low-friction after check-in and prep. Thursday, use luggage storage before the closeout and keep the 3:15 to 3:30 airport-transfer window for the 6:05-ish flight. Just do not plan around free breakfast there, since they have confirmed it is paid.
Tuesday starts early. Should I rely on the hotel restaurant for breakfast?

Only if it opens early enough and gives an itemized receipt. Safer backup: grab coffee/snack from the hotel market or a nearby cafe, or use the hospital cafeteria after arrival if timing works. I would also pack one breakfast bar so you are not stuck if the restaurant opens late.
For Wednesday, should I prebook a rideshare or just keep it as a fallback?

Keep it as a fallback for now. Ask the client by Monday afternoon for shuttle pickup time, pickup spot, driver or coordinator contact, Scottsdale drop-off point, and the expected return window. If the return is still vague by Tuesday afternoon, plan to call a rideshare after the walkthrough rather than waiting around.
Great. Give me the final pasteable checklist, including receipts.

Phoenix checklist: check in online and keep 24A outbound if no extra fee; monitor ATL weather before leaving Decatur at 7:45 Monday; use paid or backup breakfast rather than assuming it is included; confirm Wednesday shuttle details by Monday afternoon and keep rideshare as the Scottsdale fallback; use hotel luggage storage Thursday; leave campus or hotel around 3:15 to 3:30 for PHX; save flight receipt, ticket number, confirmation code, seat assignments, hotel folio with paid-breakfast language, manager approval, and all rideshare receipts.

messages.content: Phoenix is wrapped. I have a new one: early-March reporting workshop in Minneapolis, solo. Can you help me frame the plan before I go back to the client?
Sure. What is already known: dates, onsite days, likely location, arrival expectations, and whether you expect to rent a car?

Likely Monday March 3 to Thursday March 6. Tuesday and Wednesday onsite, Thursday probably a closeout. They have not confirmed whether it is the downtown hospital building or a nearby admin office. I would rather not rent a car if rideshare or transit is workable. I care about strong reviews, breakfast that does not slow me down, and dinner nearby.

Good working frame: keep both downtown/campus-adjacent and admin-office-area hotels in play until the site is confirmed. I would treat the airport area as a backup only because it adds morning uncertainty. For flights, ATL-MSP nonstops should be the first comparison set, with Monday arrival early enough for check-in and prep.
I saw Delta nonstops, but the cheaper one-stops through Chicago or Detroit are tempting on paper. March connections make me nervous.

That concern is reasonable. For this workshop, a one-stop needs to save a lot and have a comfortable connection to be worth proposing. If it is a tight winter connection or pushes arrival late Monday, the nonstop is the cleaner approval recommendation.
What outbound window would you aim for if Tuesday starts at 9?

Monday late morning to midafternoon is the best target. It gets you to Minneapolis with daylight, time for hotel check-in or bag drop, a short prep block, and dinner. A late-evening arrival would work only if Tuesday prep is already complete and the hotel is very close to the site.
Return is trickier. I do not know if Thursday closeout is noon or midafternoon.

Then hold two return scenarios: if the closeout ends near noon, a midafternoon nonstop may work; if it could run past lunch, an early-evening nonstop is safer. I would not lock a return until they confirm the expected end time.
If the site stays vague for a few days, which hotel area should I shortlist?

Shortlist downtown first, especially anything connected by skyway or a short rideshare from the hospital campus, because it also gives dinner options without a car. Keep one admin-office-area hotel as a comparison if that address is likely. I would only include an airport hotel if the downtown rates are out of bounds.
Can you list the exact questions I should send the client so this becomes approval-ready?

Send these: 1. What is the exact Tuesday/Wednesday site address? 2. What time should I be onsite Tuesday? 3. Is Wednesday a full day, and what is the expected end time? 4. What time should Thursday closeout end? 5. Do you expect me to use rideshare, transit, or a client shuttle between hotel and site? 6. Is there a preferred hotel area or negotiated property? 7. Any security check-in time I should build in? Provisional plan to note: ATL-MSP nonstop Monday late morning or midafternoon; Thursday return held until closeout time is confirmed; hotel near the confirmed site with strong guest ratings, practical breakfast, and dinner access. If they are comfortable with a review floor, I would use roughly 4.0+ guest rating and flag anything below that as a cost tradeoff.

messages.content: Update on Minneapolis: the client confirmed the downtown hospital campus. Tuesday starts at 9, Wednesday is a full workshop day, and Thursday closeout should end around noon. Can we pick the package for manager approval?

Yes. Send me the main flight and hotel options you see in the portal, especially prices and cancellation terms. The big decisions are Thursday margin and whether the hotel location is worth more than included breakfast.

Flights: A is Delta nonstop Monday 11:05 ATL to 12:45 MSP, return Thursday 3:20 MSP to Atlanta, $438. B is the same outbound but return 5:55 pm, $467. C is a one-stop through Chicago, leaves Monday 2:15, arrives 7:40, 50-minute connection, return about 5:30, $348.

Flight B is the strongest approval choice. The Monday nonstop gives you time to land, get downtown, check in or drop bags, and prep. The 5:55 return protects you if the Thursday noon closeout runs long. Flight A saves $29 but gets tight quickly. Flight C saves more, but the late arrival plus 50-minute winter connection is the wrong risk for a workshop.

Hotels: 1 is a skyway-connected downtown hotel, 4.5 guest rating, $232, on-site restaurant, paid breakfast, refundable until Friday, 10-minute indoor walk to campus. 2 is limited-service, 4.2 rating, $189, included breakfast, no full restaurant, 12-15 minute rideshare. 3 is airport area, 4.1 rating, $155, breakfast included, restaurant next door, 25-35 minute rideshare downtown.

Hotel 1 fits the confirmed site best. The skyway and on-site restaurant matter for two early onsite days and a March trip without a rental car. Hotel 2 is a reasonable savings option, but it trades included breakfast for daily rideshares and less convenient dinner. Hotel 3 is cheapest, but it creates the most morning risk and would be hard to defend with a 9 a.m. downtown start.
Breakfast is the one thing I hesitate on. Is paid breakfast worth accepting here?

For this schedule, yes, if the nightly rate is within policy. Paid breakfast is not ideal, but the 10-minute indoor walk and on-site dinner reduce more friction than the included breakfast at the farther hotel. I would mention paid breakfast clearly in the approval note so it is not a surprise.
What if my manager asks why not the airport hotel?

Use the schedule argument: the airport hotel would add a 25-35 minute rideshare each way, with weather and traffic variability, for a 9 a.m. hospital-campus start and a full Wednesday workshop. The downtown hotel reduces commute risk and removes the need for a rental car.
Could I pair Hotel 1 with the 3:20 return and save the $29?

I would not. A noon closeout rarely means you are out the door at noon exactly; you may need final questions, notes, goodbyes, bag retrieval, and the ride to MSP. The 3:20 flight is possible only if everything ends cleanly. For $29, the 5:55 return is the better work-trip margin.
Would the 11:05 outbound be too early if I have school drop-off? I can probably leave Decatur around 8:15.

An 8:15 Decatur departure should be workable for an 11:05 ATL flight if traffic and security are normal. If school drop-off slips badly, the better backup is a later nonstop, not the one-stop through Chicago. I would keep the 11:05 as the proposed flight.
Okay. Since I arrive at 12:45, should I ask the hotel for early check-in?

Yes, request early check-in but do not rely on it. The approval plan should assume bag drop at the hotel, then a prep block in the lobby, business center, or a nearby cafe until the room is ready. Also request a quiet room away from elevators.
Should I pick a window seat now?
Yes, once the itinerary is selected, choose window seats on both legs if they are available at no extra fee. But do not switch to the weaker flight just for seat availability.
Please write the package summary for approval. Include the tradeoffs and any missing confirmations.

Draft: I recommend booking the Delta nonstop ATL-MSP on Monday March 3, departing 11:05 a.m. and arriving 12:45 p.m., with the Thursday March 6 nonstop return at 5:55 p.m. The earlier 3:20 p.m. return saves only $29 but leaves limited cushion if the noon closeout runs long. The cheaper one-stop itinerary saves more but adds a tight winter connection and late Monday arrival. I recommend the skyway-connected downtown hotel near the hospital campus at $232/night, 4.5 guest rating, refundable until Friday, with on-site dining and a 10-minute indoor walk to the client site. Breakfast is paid rather than included, but the location reduces commute risk for the 9 a.m. start and avoids a rental car. Missing before purchase: final manager approval, fare still available, hotel still refundable at booking, and confirmation that Thursday closeout remains near noon.
